text: To be eligible for OSAP at Laurentian University, you must typically meet the following requirements:

text_id: ontario resident you must be an ontario resident this is generally defined by having lived in ontario for at least 12 consecutive months not including time spent as a full time post secondary student
text: Ontario Resident: You must be an Ontario resident. This is generally defined by having lived in Ontario for at least 12 consecutive months, not including time spent as a full-time post-secondary student.

text_id: approved program of study you must be enrolled in an osap approved program that leads to a degree diploma or certificate most undergraduate master s and doctoral programs at laurentian are approved if you are in a non degree program or certain specialized certificate programs it s best to confirm eligibility with laurentian s student awards office
text: Approved Program of Study: You must be enrolled in an OSAP-approved program that leads to a degree, diploma, or certificate. Most undergraduate, Master's, and Doctoral programs at Laurentian are approved. If you are in a non-degree program or certain specialized certificate programs, it's best to confirm eligibility with Laurentian's Student Awards Office.

text_id: eligible course load your registration must meet the minimum requirements for either full time or part time osap
text: Eligible Course Load: Your registration must meet the minimum requirements for either full-time or part-time OSAP.

text_id: good standing you must not be in default on any previous osap loans or have any restrictions on your osap account
text: Good Standing: You must not be in default on any previous OSAP loans or have any restrictions on your OSAP account.

text_id: satisfactory academic progress you need to maintain satisfactory academic progress in your program of study
text: Satisfactory Academic Progress: You need to maintain satisfactory academic progress in your program of study.

text_id: lifetime funding limit you must not have exceeded the lifetime limit of student loan funding typically 340 weeks for most students 400 weeks for doctoral students or up to 520 weeks for students with a permanent disability
text: Lifetime Funding Limit: You must not have exceeded the lifetime limit of student loan funding (typically 340 weeks for most students, 400 weeks for doctoral students, or up to 520 weeks for students with a permanent disability).

text_id: in order to be considered a full time student for the purpose of receiving osap funding you must meet one of the following criteria

text_id: undergraduate students must be fully registered student in at least 60 of a full time course load per term the equivalent of at least three half courses per term
text: Undergraduate students must be fully-registered student in at least 60% of a full-time course load per term (the equivalent of at least three half courses per term)

text_id: undergraduate students who have a permanent disability are eligible if enrolled in at least 40 of a full time course load per term the equivalent of at least two half courses per term
text: Undergraduate students who have a permanent disability are eligible if enrolled in at least 40% of a full-time course load per term (the equivalent of at least two half courses per term)

text_id: all full time graduate students are assessed for osap based on a 100 course load part time students are considered to be registered in a 50 course load only graduate students who self identify as having a permanent disability are eligible for full time osap at this course load
text: All full-time graduate students are assessed for OSAP based on a 100% course load. Part-time students are considered to be registered in a 50% course load. Only graduate students who self-identify as having a permanent disability are eligible for full-time OSAP at this course load.
